data.body: S1 T1 LANDED: Gerrit change 1880 submitted, status MERGED at 2026-08-19T00:34:29Z. LANDING STRATEGY DECISION recorded: AGENTS.md's Gerrit workflow rule says that when the server-side feature-branch path is unavailable to the configured identity (RebarBotNava is a Contributor, not a feature-branch-driver), the sanctioned path is to send each independently reviewable change through refs/for/main and Submit it before advancing to a dependent change - so RP-02 lands INCREMENTALLY rather than as a 9-deep relation chain, which AGENTS.md itself warns is fragile at this size. Project docs win over the skill's default end-of-run stack submit. Regression safety for this first land is trivial: T1 is purely additive (a new module plus its own new test file, with NO production caller yet - the facade cutover is T2), both gates were green, and the full 2808-test reconciler suite passed. S1 T2 test authoring done meanwhile: 7 characterization tests appended to state/test_binding_store.py covering AC1 signature stability, AC2 shallow all_bindings + pending/confirmed/reverse reload, AC3 facade-vs-repository byte parity and shared corruption disposition, AC4 peer_state/get_rotation independence, AC5 non-exposure of a writable repository. T2 is a REFACTOR, so these are characterization tests that are green before and after by design - RED-first is not the right gate for a no-behavior-change slice, so teeth were proven instead by 4 defect-seeded mutations of the facade, each of which went RED: all_bindings deep-copying, live corruption failing open, save() bypassing get_rotation, and a public signature drift on bind_confirm. 4 discriminator tests held out of the worktree (shallow-copy depth, corruption disposition parity, peer/rotation independence, repository non-exposure); 22 tests visible to the implementer plus the whole pre-existing suite as its regression oracle.
